title: api: standardize rate-limit semantics and idempotency for streaming + openai-compat
author: Jordan Kline
description:
Motivation: clients integrating via the OpenAI-compat layer and native Redwood API observed inconsistent 429/Retry-After behavior between streaming and non-streaming endpoints, and ambiguous semantics for idempotency keys with streaming/function-calling requests. This PR unifies rate-limit semantics across streaming and non-streaming paths, ensures a single canonical Retry-After header (seconds) is emitted from the gateway and proxied through the runtime, and clarifies idempotency handling for streaming/function calls.

What this changes: 1) Gateway: normalizes 429/503 responses to include a Retry-After header in seconds when available and a machine-friendly JSON body under the OpenAI-compat error schema (type, message, param). 2) Streaming: the streaming mux now emits a single terminal error event when rate-limited (instead of partial stream + ambiguous disconnect). Clients receive a final event with error and Retry-After metadata. 3) Idempotency: idempotency-key handling is extended to streaming/function-calling flows: keys are recorded when a stream/function invocation starts; duplicate requests within the idempotency window return the same terminal outcome when available or a 409 with reproducible metadata when still in progress. 4) SDK/backwards-compat: OpenAI-compat responses without Retry-After are still supported; we add defensive parsing and warn in logs rather than hard-fail. 5) Observability: new metrics (api.rate_limited.count, api.retry_after.seconds.histogram, api.idempotency.hit/miss) and tracing tags are emitted for rate-limited and idempotency flows. 6) Tests and docs: unit/integration tests for streaming 429s and idempotency; docs update in openai-compat and API error semantics.

Testing and CI: added unit tests for gateway header propagation and streaming termination; integration test simulating concurrent idempotent streaming requests; e2e against a canary runtime to validate Retry-After correctness. CI initially failed due to a flaky streaming test; fixed by stabilizing stream shutdown sequence.

Backward compatibility: we aim for compatibility with existing clients: behavior is additive (additional Retry-After header and clearer error JSON) and fallbacks preserve previous body shapes where possible. Clients parsing body fields should continue to work, but we recommend clients prefer the Retry-After header for backoff timing.

Related: ENG-3245 (rate-limit backlog), ENG-3301 (streaming reliability), PM-1122 (openai-compat error UX).
commits: feat(gateway): normalize 429/503 responses and add Retry-After header
fix(streaming): emit terminal error event on rate-limit and include retry metadata
feat(idempotency): record idempotency keys for streaming/function-calls and return consistent terminal outcomes
test: add unit + integration tests for streaming 429s and idempotency duplicates
docs(openai-compat): update error semantics and recommend Retry-After header usage
chore(sdk-python): defensive parsing for missing Retry-After and log warning
perf: add metrics for rate-limited events and retry-after histogram
review_comments: Sofia: Can we guarantee that the Retry-After header is in seconds? Some clients expect RFC-1123 dates. Please normalize to integer seconds and document it.

Author (Jordan): Normalized to seconds across gateway and documented in openai-compat.md. RFC-1123 dates may still be emitted by some upstream infra but we always translate to seconds for API responses.
Liam: Concern about memory growth for long-running streams when we record idempotency entries. Do we TTL entries aggressively?
Author: TTL set to 24h by default with configurable window; added eviction and a metric to track outstanding idempotency entries.
Arielle: Approve after CI fixes and tests stabilised. Also asked to add a dashboard tile for rate_limited count.
Author: Added Grafana tile and a brief note in release notes. CI initially failed a flaky test; fixed race in stream shutdown by adding an explicit drain step.
release_notes: Standardized rate-limit semantics (Retry-After in seconds) across streaming and non-streaming endpoints; clarified idempotency behavior for streaming and function-calling flows; added metrics for rate-limiting and idempotency; OpenAI-compat error responses now include machine-friendly fields (type/param/message).
notes: Hotfix follow-ups: a small patch (hotfix/91584-ratelimit-metrics) will be open to tweak metric labels in prod analytics based on initial rollout telemetry.
